evals.prompt: Using the Yices C API, fill a 3x3 magic square with the numbers 1 to 9 and print it.
evals.expected_output: A C program with distinct, bounded integer terms and equal line sums, printing one model
assertions: Reads interfaces/c.md
Calls yices_init() first
Uses yices_new_uninterpreted_term, not yices_new_variable
Reads values only after YICES_STATUS_SAT and frees the model

evals.prompt: Write a C program with Yices that lists all solutions of 6 queens.
evals.expected_output: Every placement via a no-good loop ending in UNSAT
assertions: Reads interfaces/c.md
Asserts a disjunction of output differences after each model
Does not use yices_assert_blocking_clause
Stops on YICES_STATUS_UNSAT

evals.prompt: In C with Yices, maximise the value of a 0/1 knapsack read from a JSON file.
evals.expected_output: Tightening loop proving the optimum
assertions: Reads interfaces/c.md
Asserts objective > best after each SAT
Reports the optimum only after UNSAT
Reads JSON with a library such as cJSON, links -lyices

evals.prompt: Using Yices from C, find integers x, y with x*y = 91 and 1 < x < y.
evals.expected_output: A QF_NIA context
assertions: Reads interfaces/c.md
Creates the context from yices_default_config_for_logic with QF_NIA
Does not use the default context for the product

evals.prompt: Write a Python program with the yices package that finds all optimal splits of a list of numbers into two equal-count groups with minimal sum difference.
evals.expected_output: Optimum by tightening, then all optima in a fresh Context
assertions: Reads interfaces/python.md
Builds expressions with Terms.*, not Python operators
Uses a new Context with objective == best and a no-good loop
Compares status with Status.SAT / Status.UNSAT

evals.prompt: Using Yices in Python, schedule jobs on machines to minimise the makespan with a 10 second limit.
evals.expected_output: Disjunctive scheduling with a bound loop and a timeout
assertions: Reads interfaces/python.md
Uses check_context(timeout=...)
Treats Status.INTERRUPTED as not proven optimal
Uses Terms.yor for the no-overlap disjunction

evals.prompt: Show that 5 pigeons cannot go into 4 holes with Yices in Python.
evals.expected_output: UNSAT reported as infeasible
assertions: Reads interfaces/python.md
Uses Terms.distinct or pairwise disequalities
Does not read a model after UNSAT

evals.prompt: Use Yices to find a feasible assignment for a small integer scheduling problem.
evals.expected_output: The interface table routes to one binding and the model is written
assertions: Reads SKILL.md and one interface file
Uses uninterpreted terms and checks the status before reading the model

evals.prompt: Write a C program with Yices that finds all optimal splits of a list of numbers into two equal-count groups with minimal sum difference.
evals.expected_output: Optimum by tightening, then all optima in a fresh context
assertions: Reads interfaces/c.md
Builds a new context with objective == best
Enumerates with a no-good loop ending in UNSAT
Frees models and contexts

evals.prompt: Using the Yices C API, colour a graph read from an edge list with as few colours as possible.
evals.expected_output: Minimisation by a decreasing bound loop
assertions: Reads interfaces/c.md
Asserts objective < best after each SAT
Reports optimal only after UNSAT
Checks every builder result for NULL_TERM

evals.prompt: In C with Yices, schedule jobs on machines to minimise the makespan, with a time limit.
evals.expected_output: Disjunctive scheduling with a bound loop and a timer-based stop
assertions: Reads interfaces/c.md
Uses yices_or of two ordering atoms for no-overlap
Uses yices_stop_search from a signal timer for the limit
Treats YICES_STATUS_INTERRUPTED as not proven optimal

evals.prompt: In C with the Yices API, write a solver for a cryptarithm read from a JSON file such as {"addends": ["SEND", "MORE"], "sum": "MONEY"}: one distinct digit per letter, no leading zero on a multi-letter word.
evals.expected_output: Constraints built from the data: letter terms bounded 0..9, distinct, weighted sums for each word
assertions: Reads interfaces/c.md
Takes the letters and words from the JSON data, nothing hard-coded
Builds each word as a weighted sum of letter terms and asserts the addition as an equality
Asserts distinct over the letters and non-zero leading letters
Reads values only after SAT, and reports no assignment when the status is UNSAT

evals.prompt: In C with the Yices API, place n queens on an n by n board for n given as input (for example 8, and also 3 which has no placement) and print one placement or say that none exists.
evals.expected_output: One placement via distinct columns and diagonal disequalities; infeasible read from UNSAT
assertions: Reads interfaces/c.md
Uses distinct for columns and disequalities on differences for diagonals
Takes n from the input
Reports infeasible from UNSAT and reads no model then
Reads values only after SAT
